title: console
lede: Node-console-shaped logging for CLI tools and services. The full print family works; the one remaining print-path divergence is console.trace, which prints only its message with no stack walk. console.time tracks each label independently via a per-label backing map, matching console.count. console.table renders Node's exact Unicode box-drawing table for arrays of objects or primitives (other shapes fall back to console.log).

entries.name: console.log(...)
entries.description: Writes its arguments to stdout on one line, joined by single spaces, followed by a newline. A no-argument call prints a bare newline, and -0 displays as -0 (matching Node's util.inspect display, even though String(-0) stays "0").
differences: A printed string is written via `printf`'s `"%s"`, so a value with an embedded null byte truncates *on display* at the first `\0` — the stored string is intact (`.length` and every operation see the full bytes); a binary-safe `fwrite` print is deferred as display-only, low-value. Use `process.stdout.write` for binary output

entries.name: console.error(...)
entries.description: Like console.log, but writes to stderr instead of stdout.

entries.name: console.warn(...)
entries.description: Writes to stderr, unprefixed — identical to console.error, exactly as real Node treats it.

entries.name: console.info(...)
entries.description: Alias for console.log — writes to stdout on one line.

entries.name: console.debug(...)
entries.description: Alias for console.log — writes to stdout on one line.

entries.name: console.trace(...)
entries.description: Prints "Trace: <message>" to stderr through the same generic print path as console.debug/info — with no stack-walking logic.
differences: Prints `"Trace: <message>"` and nothing else; real Node's entire point of `.trace()` is the call stack it prints below the message, which this never generates at all

entries.name: console.assert(cond, msg)
entries.description: Writes an assertion failure message when cond is falsy; does nothing when cond is truthy.

entries.name: console.table()
entries.description: Renders an array of objects (one column per shared field) or an array of primitives (a single Values column) as Node's Unicode box-drawing table — byte-for-byte the same layout Node v26 produces, with dynamic per-column widths, left-aligned cells, and quoted string cells.
differences: A `columns` filter argument, a plain-object argument, and an array-of-arrays shape aren't tabulated — they fall back to `console.log`, as a non-tabular value does.

entries.name: console.time() / .timeEnd()
entries.signature: time(label?: string): void; timeEnd(label?: string): void
entries.description: Starts a monotonic timer with time() and prints the elapsed "label: <N>ms" with timeEnd(). An omitted label is exactly "default", matching real Node. Distinct labels track independent timers via a per-label backing map.

entries.name: console.count() / .countReset()
entries.signature: count(label?: string): void; countReset(label?: string): void
entries.description: count() prints "label: <n>" with a per-label counter that increments each call; countReset() zeroes one label. Backed by a real Map<string, number>, so it matches real Node's per-label semantics exactly — unlike time's single-slot narrowing.
entries.snippet:
console.count()            // default: 1
console.count('apples')    // apples: 1
console.countReset('apples')
console.count('apples')    // apples: 1

entries.name: console.group() / .groupEnd()
entries.description: Indents every subsequent console.* line by two spaces per nesting level. An unbalanced extra groupEnd() floors at depth 0 rather than going negative.

entries.name: console.dir()
entries.signature: dir(value: any, options?: { depth?: number | null; colors?: boolean }): void
entries.description: Prints a single value like a single-argument console.log, at Node's util.inspect default nesting depth of 2. The depth option overrides it (a number caps nesting, null is unlimited); beyond the cap a nested value shows as [Object]/[Array].
differences: The `colors` option is accepted but ignored — inspected output carries no ANSI here.
